children.name: Campylorhynchus
children.description: The largest wrens, boldly patterned with streaked or barred plumage and notably loud, chattering duets. Found from the southwestern United States through Central America and northern South America, often in arid scrub, cactus desert, and forest edge. Several species are highly social and cooperative breeders.

children.name: Campylorhynchus brunneicapillus
children.description: The cactus wren (Campylorhynchus brunneicapillus) is a species of wren that is endemic to the deserts of the southwestern United States and northern and central Mexico.

children.name: Campylorhynchus chiapensis
children.description: The giant wren (Campylorhynchus chiapensis) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.

children.name: Campylorhynchus fasciatus
children.description: The fasciated wren (Campylorhynchus fasciatus) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.

children.name: Campylorhynchus griseus
children.description: The bicolored wren (Campylorhynchus griseus) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.

children.name: Campylorhynchus gularis
children.description: The spotted wren (Campylorhynchus gularis) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.

children.name: Campylorhynchus jocosus
children.description: Boucard's wren (Campylorhynchus jocosus) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae. It is endemic to Mexico.

children.name: Campylorhynchus nuchalis
children.description: The stripe-backed wren (Campylorhynchus nuchalis) is a bird found in the savannas of northern Colombia and central Venezuela. It lives in dry, riparian woodland, or farmlands, and is found at heights up to 800 m.

children.name: Campylorhynchus rufinucha
children.description: The Veracruz wren (Campylorhynchus rufinucha) is a songbird of the family Troglodytidae.

children.name: Campylorhynchus turdinus
children.description:
The thrush-like wren (Campylorhynchus turdinus) is a South American species of bird in the family Troglodytidae, the wrens. As suggested by its common and scientific name, its size and coloration are vaguely reminiscent of that of a thrush, although the general impression it gives in life is very different and not at all "thrush-like".
With a total length of approximately 20 cm (8 in), it is among the largest species of wrens. The head and mantle are brownish-gray. The wings and upper tail are dull brown with dense blackish barring. The whitish underparts are heavily spotted with dusky, except on the throat. It typically shows a distinctive whitish eyebrow and the relatively long tail is commonly held cocked. The slightly decurved bill is relatively long, and, for a wren, thick. The irides are dull amber, maroon or brown.

children.name: Campylorhynchus unicolor
children.description: A plain grey-brown, unstreaked Campylorhynchus restricted to the cloud forest edges and humid montane scrub of the western Andes in Ecuador and northern Peru. It is the most range-restricted member of its genus and among the least-studied. Its subdued plumage and quiet habits make it easy to overlook.

children.name: Campylorhynchus zonatus
children.description:
The band-backed wren (Campylorhynchus zonatus) is a small songbird of the wren family.
The band-backed wren is a resident breeding species from south-central Gulf Coast Mexico to northwestern Ecuador. It occurs in five disjunct areas, the central region being in southern Central America, in Costa Rica and northern Panama. The next two regions are northern Colombia adjacent to Panama, and 800 km to the south in northwestern Ecuador.

children.name: Campylorhynchus yucatanicus
children.description: The Yucatan wren (Campylorhynchus yucatanicus) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.

children.name: Campylorhynchus megalopterus
children.description: The gray-barred wren (Campylorhynchus megalopterus) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae. It is endemic to Mexico.

children.name: Campylorhynchus albobrunneus
children.description: The white-headed wren (Campylorhynchus albobrunneus) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae. It is found in Colombia and Panama.

children.name: Campylorhynchus barroti
children.description: A heavily streaked, dark-capped wren of humid foothill and lowland forest in Panama and Colombia. It was long treated as a subspecies of the Band-backed Wren but is now recognised as a full species based on plumage and vocal differences. Like its congeners, it is a cooperative breeder living in extended family groups.

children.name: Salpinctes
children.description: A monotypic genus of rocky desert wrens found throughout the arid interior of western North America. Rock Wrens are highly adapted to life among boulders and cliff faces, where they construct pebble pavements leading to their nests.

children.name: Salpinctes obsoletus
children.description: The rock wren (Salpinctes obsoletus) is a small songbird of the wren family native to the rocky areas of western North America.

children.name: Catherpes
children.description: A monotypic genus of canyon-dwelling wrens with a remarkably long, decurved bill used to probe crevices in cliff faces and rocky outcrops in western North America.

children.name: Catherpes mexicanus
children.description: The canyon wren (Catherpes mexicanus) is a small North American songbird of the wren family Troglodytidae.

children.name: Hylorchilus
children.description: Two rare and poorly known wrens endemic to Mexico, associated with limestone karst outcrops and forested ravines. Both species have restricted ranges and are considered vulnerable or near-threatened.

children.name: Hylorchilus sumichrasti
children.description: Sumichrast's wren (Hylorchilus sumichrasti), also known as the slender-billed wren, is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae. It is endemic to Mexico.

children.name: Hylorchilus navai
children.description: Nava's wren (Hylorchilus navai) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae. It is endemic to Mexico.

children.name: Cistothorus
children.description: Marsh and grassland wrens of the Americas, typically skulking in dense vegetation and difficult to observe despite their loud, mechanical songs. Several species are marsh obligates, nesting among cattails and sedges over standing water.

children.name: Cistothorus platensis
children.description: The grass wren (Cistothorus platensis) is a species of passerine bird in the family Troglodytidae. It is widely distributed in central and southern America.

children.name: Cistothorus apolinari
children.description: Apolinar's wren (Cistothorus apolinari) is a passerine bird in the family Troglodytidae. It is endemic to Colombia.

children.name: Cistothorus meridae
children.description: The Mérida wren (Cistothorus meridae), or paramo wren, is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae. It is endemic to Venezuela.

children.name: Cistothorus stellaris
children.description: The sedge wren (Cistothorus stellaris) is a small and secretive passerine bird in the family Troglodytidae.

children.name: Cistothorus palustris
children.description: The marsh wren is a small North American songbird of the wren family. It was formerly called the long-billed marsh wren to distinguish it from the sedge wren, then known as the short-billed marsh wren.

children.name: Thryomanes
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Bewick's Wren, a widespread and adaptable wren of western North America known for its exceptionally varied and musical song.

children.name: Thryomanes bewickii
children.description:
Bewick's wren (Thryomanes bewickii) is a wren native to North America. It is the only species placed in the genus Thryomanes. At about long, it is grey-brown above, white below, with a long white eyebrow. While similar in appearance to the Carolina wren, it has a long tail that is tipped in white. The song is loud and melodious, much like the song of other wrens. It lives in thickets, brush piles and hedgerows, open woodlands and scrubby areas, often near streams. It eats insects and spiders, which it gleans from vegetation or finds on the ground.
Its historic range was from southern British Columbia, Nebraska, southern Ontario, and southwestern Pennsylvania, Maryland, south to Mexico, Arkansas and the northern Gulf States. However, it is now extremely rare east of the Mississippi River.

children.name: Thryophilus
children.description: Middle American and northern South American wrens of forest edge and thickets, characterised by warm rufous or brown tones and often bold face patterns. Several species are restricted to narrow geographic ranges.

children.name: Thryophilus pleurostictus
children.description: The banded wren (Thryophilus pleurostictus) is a small songbird of the wren family.

children.name: Thryophilus rufalbus
children.description:
The rufous-and-white wren (Thryophilus rufalbus) is a small songbird of the wren family. It is a resident breeding species from southwesternmost Mexico to northern Colombia and northwestern Venezuela. It was formerly placed in the genus Thryothorus (Mann et al., 2006).
This large wren breeds in lowlands and foothills from sea level up to altitude in dry forests or, in wetter areas, more open scrubby woodland. In Central America, it mainly occurs on the Pacific side of the central mountain ranges Its flask-shaped nest is constructed high in a tree or shrub. The female alone incubates the three or four greenish-blue eggs for about two weeks to hatching, and the young fledge in about the same length of time again.

children.name: Thryophilus spadix
children.description: A dark-capped, rufous-brown wren of humid lowland and foothill forest in Panama and northwestern Colombia, associated with dense undergrowth near streams and forest edges. It was long considered a subspecies of the Rufous-and-white Wren but differs in its dark sooty-grey head and more restricted range. Its loud duets are characteristic sounds of wet lowland forest.

children.name: Thryophilus nicefori
children.description:
Niceforo's wren (Thryophilus nicefori) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae. It is endemic to Colombia.
Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical high-altitude dry shrubland. It is threatened by habitat loss.

children.name: Pheugopedius
children.description: A genus of mostly Middle American and northern South American wrens with boldly patterned faces and rich, complex songs. Many species were formerly placed in Thryothorus; molecular analysis prompted a widespread reclassification.

children.name: Pheugopedius euophrys
children.description: The plain-tailed wren (Pheugopedius euophrys) is a species of songbird in the family Troglodytidae. It has a mostly rufous body with a gray, black, and white striped head. It is found in the Andes of southern Colombia, Ecuador, and northern Peru. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forests. Plain-tailed wrens are so-called bamboo specialists and live almost exclusively in chusquea bamboo thickets. Like other wrens, its diet consists mainly of insects with some seeds and berries.

children.name: Pheugopedius eisenmanni
children.description: }} The Inca wren (Pheugopedius eisenmanni) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.

children.name: Pheugopedius atrogularis
children.description: The black-throated wren (Pheugopedius atrogularis) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae. It is found in Costa Rica, Nicaragua, and Panama.

children.name: Pheugopedius genibarbis
children.description: The moustached wren (Pheugopedius genibarbis) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.

children.name: Pheugopedius felix
children.description: The happy wren (Pheugopedius felix) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.

children.name: Pheugopedius maculipectus
children.description: The spot-breasted wren (Pheugopedius maculipectus) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae. It is found in Belize, Costa Rica, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Mexico, and Nicaragua.

children.name: Pheugopedius mystacalis
children.description: | range_map = Pheugopedius mystacalis map.svg.

children.name: Pheugopedius coraya
children.description: | range_map = Pheugopedius coraya map.svg.

children.name: Pheugopedius rutilus
children.description: The rufous-breasted wren (Pheugopedius rutilus) is a small songbird of the family Troglodytidae. It is found in Colombia, Costa Rica, Panama, Trinidad and Tobago, and Venezuela.

children.name: Pheugopedius schlegelii
children.description: Named after the Dutch ornithologist Hermann Schlegel, this Andean foothills wren ranges from Colombia to Bolivia in humid subtropical and tropical forest undergrowth. Its speckled breast and streaked head distinguish it from similar congeners. It is most often encountered in dense tangled vegetation along forest borders and ravines.

children.name: Pheugopedius sclateri
children.description: The speckle-breasted wren (Pheugopedius sclateri) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae. It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

children.name: Pheugopedius solstitialis
children.description: A richly streaked wren of Andean cloud forest in Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru, often encountered in bamboo-dominated undergrowth and dense forest borders at 1,500–2,800 m. Its strongly streaked throat distinguishes it from most congeners. Pairs produce interlocking antiphonal duets that ring through the cloud forest.

children.name: Thryothorus
children.description: The largest wren genus in terms of species richness outside of Campylorhynchus reclassification, centred on the Americas. Carolina Wrens and their allies are noted for their powerful, musical songs and strong pair bonds maintained throughout the year.

children.name: Thryothorus ludovicianus
children.description: The Carolina wren is a species of wren common in the eastern United States, the extreme south of Ontario, Canada, the northeast and southeast of Mexico, and into northern Central America. Severe winters restrict the northern limits of their range, while favorable weather conditions lead to a northward extension of their breeding range. Their preferred habitat is in dense cover in forest, farm edges, and suburban areas.

children.name: Thryothorus nigricapillus
children.description: The bay wren (Cantorchilus nigricapillus) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.

children.name: Thryothorus superciliaris
children.description: }} The superciliated wren (Cantorchilus superciliaris) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.

children.name: Thryothorus galbraithii
children.description: Named after the British ornithologist John Galbraith, this Colombian endemic inhabits dense undergrowth in humid lowland forest on the Pacific slope of the western Andes. It is poorly known and rarely observed, with few modern records confirming its occurrence outside of the type locality. Its conservation status is considered near-threatened owing to ongoing deforestation.

children.name: Thryothorus semibadius
children.description: The riverside wren (Cantorchilus semibadius) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.

children.name: Thryothorus atricapilloides
children.description: The Pale-breasted Wren inhabits the arid coastal scrub, dry interior valleys, and thorn woodland of Peru, Ecuador, and extreme northern Chile. Its paler, buff-white underparts and less distinct facial markings distinguish it from the Buff-breasted Wren, which replaces it in more humid habitats to the north. It is among the most drought-tolerant wrens and can be found in some of the driest coastal desert scrub in South America.

children.name: Troglodytes
children.description: For their size, wrens produce one of the loudest songs of any bird — a rapid powerful torrent of trills carrying hundreds of metres through dense cover. In harsh Scandinavian winters dozens of wrens will huddle together in a nest box for warmth. One of Sweden's most widespread and numerous species despite its tiny size.

children.name: Troglodytes troglodytes
children.description: The Eurasian wren is a very small insectivorous bird and the only member of the wren family found in the Old World, specifically in Eurasia and Africa (Maghreb). In Anglophone Europe, it is commonly known simply as the wren. It has a very short tail which is often held erect, a short neck and a relatively long thin bill.

children.name: Troglodytes aedon
children.description: The northern house wren (Troglodytes aedon) is a very small passerine in the wren family Troglodytidae.

children.name: Troglodytes musculus
children.description: The southern house wren (Troglodytes musculus) is a very small passerine bird in the wren family Troglodytidae. It is found from southern Mexico to southern Chile and southern Argentina. The name troglodytes means "hole dweller", and is a reference to the bird's tendency to disappear into crevices when hunting insects or to seek shelter. It was formerly considered to be conspecific with the northern house wren (Troglodytes aedon).

children.name: Troglodytes solstitialis
children.description: The mountain wren (Troglodytes solstitialis) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.

children.name: Troglodytes monticola
children.description: The Santa Marta wren (Troglodytes monticola) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae. It is endemic to Colombia.

children.name: Troglodytes rufulus
children.description: The tepui wren (Troglodytes rufulus) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.

children.name: Troglodytes sissonii
children.description: The Socorro wren (Troglodytes sissonii) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.

children.name: Troglodytes tanneri
children.description: The Clarión wren (Troglodytes tanneri) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae. The species is endemic to Clarión Island off Pacific Mexico.

children.name: Troglodytes cobbi
children.description:
Cobb's wren (Troglodytes cobbi) is a fairly small (12-13.5 cm) wren which is endemic to the Falkland Islands. It was formerly classified as a subspecies of the southern house wren but is now commonly considered to be a separate species due to differences in plumage, voice, ecology and morphology.
The scientific and common names commemorate Arthur Cobb, an author from the Falkland Islands.

children.name: Uropsila
children.description: A monotypic genus of small, round wrens of the forest understorey of Mexico and Central America, related to Henicorhina and sharing its skull-like creeping behaviour through dense tangles.

children.name: Uropsila leucogastra
children.description: The white-bellied wren (Uropsila leucogastra) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae. It is found in Belize, Guatemala, Honduras, and Mexico.

children.name: Henicorhina
children.description: The Wood-Wrens are small, almost tailless wrens of the Neotropical montane forest understorey, renowned for their extraordinarily powerful and melodious songs. Several recently described species occupy very narrow altitudinal and geographic ranges in the Andes.

children.name: Henicorhina leucosticta
children.description: The white-breasted wood wren (Henicorhina leucosticta) is a small songbird of the wren family. It is a resident breeding species from central Mexico to northeastern Peru and Suriname.

children.name: Henicorhina leucophrys
children.description: The grey-breasted wood wren (Henicorhina leucophrys) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae. It is found from Mexico to Bolivia.

children.name: Henicorhina leucoptera
children.description: The bar-winged wood wren (Henicorhina leucoptera) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae. It is found in southern Ecuador and northern Peru.

children.name: Henicorhina negreti
children.description: The Munchique wood wren (Henicorhina negreti) is a member of the wren family (Troglodytidae) that was described as new to science in 2003. It is found in the Western Andes of Colombia.

children.name: Henicorhina anachoreta
children.description: The hermit wood wren or Santa Marta wood wren (Henicorhina anachoreta) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae. It is endemic to the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta of northern Colombia.

children.name: Henicorhina darienensis
children.description: The Darien Wood-Wren was described in 2012 and is restricted to the cloud forests of the Darien region on the Colombia-Panama border. It had long been overlooked due to its superficial similarity to the Gray-breasted Wood-Wren but is now recognised as a distinct species based on song differences and genetic evidence. The Darien region's inaccessibility has contributed to the late discovery of this species.

children.name: Henicorhina bangsi
children.description: Named in honour of the American ornithologist Outram Bangs, this wood-wren is a Colombian endemic associated with the cloud forests of the Western and Central Andes. It has a very restricted distribution and is considered near-threatened due to extensive deforestation within its range. Recent molecular work supports its recognition as a species distinct from the Gray-breasted Wood-Wren.

children.name: Microcerculus
children.description: The nightingale-wrens are tiny, almost tailless wrens of the humid Neotropical forest floor, noted for their extraordinarily long, pure-toned songs. They creep through leaf litter and among roots on the forest floor in the manner of mice.

children.name: Microcerculus marginatus
children.description: The southern nightingale-wren (Microcerculus marginatus), also known as the scaly-breasted wren, is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae. It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Panama, Peru, and Venezuela.

children.name: Microcerculus bambla
children.description: The wing-banded wren (Microcerculus bambla) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae. It is found in Brazil, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Peru, Suriname, and Venezuela.

children.name: Microcerculus ustulatus
children.description: The flutist wren (Microcerculus ustulatus) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.

children.name: Microcerculus philomela
children.description: The northern nightingale-wren (Microcerculus philomela), or nightingale wren, is a species of passerine bird in the family Troglodytidae. It is found in Belize, Costa Rica, Guatemala, Honduras, Mexico, and Nicaragua.

children.name: Cinnycerthia
children.description: The fulvous wrens are a group of large, richly coloured wrens of Andean cloud forests and high-elevation scrub. Closely related to the wood-wrens, they differ in their larger size and typically plain or lightly streaked rufous-brown plumage.

children.name: Cinnycerthia unirufa
children.description: The rufous wren (Cinnycerthia unirufa) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.

children.name: Cinnycerthia peruana
children.description: The Peruvian wren (Cinnycerthia peruana) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.

children.name: Cinnycerthia olivascens
children.description: The sepia-brown wren or Sharpe's wren (Cinnycerthia olivascens) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae. It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

children.name: Cinnycerthia fulva
children.description: The fulvous wren (Cinnycerthia fulva) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.

children.name: Cinnycerthia cerverai
children.description: Named after the Spanish ornithologist Francisco Javier Cervera, the Sepia-brown Wren is the most recently described member of the genus, known from the cloud forests of northern Peru. It is distinguished from other Cinnycerthia by its darker, more uniformly sepia-brown plumage with less rufous tones. Its restricted range and specialised cloud forest habitat place it among Peru's most threatened passerines.

children.name: Odontorchilus
children.description: Two unusual wrens of the Neotropical forest canopy and sub-canopy, unique in the family for their predominantly arboreal, treetop-foraging habits. Both species are rarely encountered at lower levels.

children.name: Odontorchilus cinereus
children.description: The tooth-billed wren (Odontorchilus cinereus) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae. It is found in Bolivia and Brazil.

children.name: Odontorchilus branickii
children.description: The grey-mantled wren (Odontorchilus branickii) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae. It is found in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

children.name: Cyphorhinus
children.description: The song-wrens of the Neotropical forest floor and understorey, celebrated for producing some of the most hauntingly beautiful songs in the bird world. Their complex, organlike music has been compared to human choral singing.

children.name: Cyphorhinus aradus
children.description: The musician wren or organ wren (Cyphorhinus arada) is a species of wren named for its elaborate song.

children.name: Cyphorhinus modulator
children.description: The musician wren or organ wren (Cyphorhinus arada) is a species of wren named for its elaborate song.

children.name: Cyphorhinus phaeocephalus
children.description: The song wren (Cyphorhinus phaeocephalus) is a species of bird in the family Troglodytidae.

children.name: Cyphorhinus thoracicus
children.description: The southern chestnut-breasted wren (Cyphorhinus thoracicus) is a species of passerine bird in the wren family Troglodytidae that is found in southern Peru and the extreme northwest of Bolivia. It was formerly considered to be conspecific with the northern chestnut-breasted wren (Cyphorhinus dichrous) with the English name "chestnut-breasted wren".

children.name: Donacobius
children.description: A monotypic genus of a strikingly patterned marsh bird of South America, sometimes placed in its own family Donacobiidae. The Black-capped Donacobius is unique in combining a wren-like body plan with social complexity and vocal duetting reminiscent of Old World babblers.

children.name: Donacobius atricapilla
children.description: The black-capped donacobius (Donacobius atricapilla) is a conspicuous, vocal South American bird and the only bird in the genus Donacobius and family Donacobiidae. It is distributed across the northern half of South America.
